summary: Teams research and evaluate an ethical challenge based on a provided case study, submit a research paper, complete an objective test, and deliver a presentation highlighting proposed solutions and lessons learned. The event is judged virtually, and top teams advance to present to judges and may be invited to the National Leadership Conference.
time_limits: Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes
Presentation lasted no more than ten (10) minutes
Presentation will be stopped at 10 minutes
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
submission_requirements: Team submitted one (1) combined PDF file containing the Research Paper, Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual and BPA Release Form(s)
Team ID is required for all submissions
Materials from non-registered members and/or those missing team ID cannot be accepted
The team is responsible for securing a BPA Release Form(s) from any person, including themselves, whose image or work is used in the project
The team is responsible for citing all sources, including themselves, on the Works Cited page for any work used on the project
Materials must follow the organization’s BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
deadlines: The registration deadline is no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, on December 1, 2026
Submit the combined PDF file to https://upload.bpa.org no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on January 15, 2027
competencies: Demonstrate integrity and accountability by adhering consistently to ethical principles, acting with honesty and fairness, and taking responsibility for the decisions and consequences that result from those actions
Apply transparent communication practices by clearly articulating the rationale behind decisions, developing and conveying an ethical vision, and ensuring stakeholders are informed and aligned
Demonstrate empathy by considering the perspectives, feelings, and needs of others in the decision-making process, treating all individuals with compassion and respect
Apply objectivity by grounding decisions in facts, evidence, and rational analysis, actively avoiding personal bias, favoritism, and self-interest
Demonstrate courage by making and defending difficult decisions that uphold ethical principles, even in the face of opposition, pressure, or potential negative consequences
Promote collaboration and inclusion by engaging stakeholders, seeking diverse perspectives, and fostering a participatory decision-making process that leads to fair and well-informed outcomes

Demonstrate adaptability and a commitment to continuous learning by remaining open to new information, feedback, and emerging ethical trends, and adjusting decisions when necessary to uphold ethical standards

Demonstrate ethical awareness by recognizing when a decision carries ethical weight, identifying concerns embedded in problems framed as technical, operational, or financial, and surfacing them before they become consequential

Apply legal and regulatory literacy by identifying the laws, disclosure requirements, and professional standards relevant to a decision, and by complying with their intent rather than only their letter
Apply stakeholder and consequence analysis by identifying all parties affected by a decision, including those absent from it, and by evaluating both immediate and long-term impacts

rubric.description: Provides a compelling, well-supported summary that frames the ethical challenge.
Shows deep insight and thoughtful engagement with the ethical topic.
Ideas are well-developed, insightful, and supported with strong ethical reasoning.
Presents a unique and innovative ethical perspective with rich, varied sources.
Analysis is compelling, well-reasoned, and demonstrates ethical leadership.
Contains very few or no grammar or spelling errors.

rubric.criterion: Team followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy.

rubric.description: The introduction is engaging and well-structured, and the summary provides a clear, insightful wrap-up that reinforces key findings.
Content is insightful, well-developed, and strongly supports the presentation goals.
Delivery is polished, engaging, and enhances the impact of the presentation.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.

judging_notes: Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring
eligibility_notes: Any middle level, secondary, or postsecondary contestant may enter this event
A team will consist of 2–4 contestants
There are no restrictions on the number of entries per chapter or per state
Teams that do not submit an entry following the topic listed below or do not follow the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy will be disqualified
Contestants participating in the competition must be registered for the event prior to the submission deadline to be eligible
Only the team captain should complete the submission
